faq.q: What makes a team work well?
faq.a: A shared goal, clear jobs, listening to every idea and helping each other. Good teams also say thank you and sort out disagreements calmly.
asks: Tell me about the Our bridge model

faq.q: Why do team members have different jobs?
faq.a: Jobs make sure every part gets done and everyone is included. People can also use what they are best at, like drawing or measuring.
asks: Tell me about the Aiko: planner

faq.q: What if someone in my team does not help?
faq.a: Ask kindly what they would like to do, and offer a job that suits them. If it still does not work, tell your teacher.
asks: Tell me about the Raj: checker
Someone in my group is lazy

faq.q: What if we disagree on an idea?
faq.a: Let each person explain their idea, then vote, or mix the best parts of both ideas together.
asks: How do we choose between ideas?

faq.q: How can I be a good team member?
faq.a: Do your job, listen, share your ideas kindly, and help when someone is stuck. Saying well done to others helps a lot too.
asks: How do I help my group?

facts: Scientists found that northern bald ibises flying in a V formation take turns at the front, sharing the tiring lead position (Voelkl and colleagues, 2015).
A football team has 11 players on the pitch, and each one has a different job, such as goalkeeper, defender or striker.
